Class 1 · Chapter 3 of 8

Picture and number patterns

Spot what repeats and what comes next.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Add, subtract and find the missing part. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can fill a missing picture.
  • I can continue a growing pattern.
  • I can find a missing number or letter.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

A pattern repeats

Red, blue, red, blue, red, blue.

The piece 'red, blue' keeps coming round. That piece is the repeat unit.

Screen 2 of 4

Find the missing piece

Say the pattern from the start. Listen for where it repeats.

Red, blue, red, ... The next one must be blue.

Screen 3 of 4

Number patterns jump

2, 4, 6, 8 ... Each number is 2 more than the one before.

That is skip counting by twos. The next number is 10.

Screen 4 of 4

Patterns that grow

A growing pattern gets bigger each time.

1 counter, then 2, then 3, then 4. Each step adds one more.

Words to know
pattern
Something that repeats in the same order.
repeat unit
The small piece that comes round again and again.
skip counting
Counting in jumps, like 2, 4, 6, 8.

Chapter passed. Next: Shapes and solid objects

For parents

What your child learns

A pattern may repeat or it may grow. Skip counting by 2s goes 27, 29, 31. A growing pattern adds the same amount each stage. Find the step, then continue.

A common slip

Children may guess the next item without checking the step. Write the difference between neighbours. If every difference is the same, use it to fill the gap.

5-minute home activity: Growing tiles

  1. Make stage 1 with 3 paper squares.
  2. Make stage 2 with 5 squares and stage 3 with 7.
  3. Say how many squares are added each time.
  4. Predict stage 5, then build it to check.
